subject: Recap: Porting readiness for Novamed — next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@novamed.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Porting readiness for Novamed — next steps

Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move toward a low-friction POC. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you called out:
- High per-token cost on current OpenAI/Anthropic spend (~$42k/mo) with unpredictable spikes from chat assistants.
- Latency sensitive customer workflows (sub-400ms p95) for interactive triage UI.
- Auditability & data retention requirements for regulated PII flows (retention controls + KMS).

Current stack (what you shared):
- Model access: OpenAI (gpt-4o-like), Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows.
- Orchestration: in-house gateway that fans out to providers; 2k RPS peak, bursty.
- Hosting: primary prod in us-east-1; some on-prem processing for PHI ingestion.

Success criteria for a migration/porting project:
- <=20% increase in latency at p95 vs today (target: maintain <400ms).
- Unit cost reduction goal: 30–40% on comparable quality prompts.
- No disruption to compliance posture: key management + audit trails preserved.

Compatibility constraints you emphasized:
- Must support function/tool calling & structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers.
- Tokenization differences are acceptable but we need a quick-quality-check harness.
- SRE needs a non-production copy to validate rate-limiting and egress rules.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial recommendation):
- high-quality instruct base (quantized) for majority of assistant traffic (cost-first).
- a larger LLM variant for high-context clinical summarization tasks.
I noted Anthropic shapes some failure modes we should validate; we’ll include those prompts in the eval set.

Next immediate steps / owners:
1) I’ll share a lightweight migration worksheet + the usage export you provided (attached) for us to baseline costs — ACTION: Jonas (today).
2) Schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with your SRE + our solutions engineer to map network egress and vault/KMS integration — OWNER: Ben (by Tue).
3) Monica to provide POC runbook and a sandbox image (non-prod) we can stand up in your environment — OWNER: Monica (by Thu).
4) We’ll draft a pricing/effort estimate for a 6-week port + POC and circulate — OWNER: Jonas (EOD Wed).

Attachments: novamed-usage-export.csv (you shared), redwood-porting-worksheet.xlsx (incoming).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
P.S. If the SRE team prefers, we can also run an isolated POC in our Dedicated environment and provide metrics to compare against your baseline before any on-prem work.

From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@novamed.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamed SRE <sre@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Porting readiness for Novamed — next steps

Thanks Jonas — this is a helpful write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Confirming current monthly token spend is ~42k USD (avg), but we saw two spikes last month to ~85k due to research experiments.
- Latency target is hard: our UI needs p95 < 400ms; p99 can be higher during sync operations.
- Compliance: we use AWS KMS for key management. Any solution needs to either support a customer-managed key or a way to sidecar redaction before egress.

SRE (copied) — can you confirm preferred windows for a tech deep-dive? We typically do >10am PT. Also want to share a small list of prompts our assistant uses (I'll attach).

On the sandbox vs Dedicated: we'd like a sandbox in our VPC first to test egress/KMS. If that proves out, we can look at a Dedicated commitment.

Attachments: novamed-soc2-summary.pdf, novamed-prompt-samples.txt

—Claire
Claire Zhao
Head of Product, Novamed
claire.zhao@novamed.com
